sentences.text: The genus name Bathyspondylus combines the Greek words for 'deep' and 'vertebra'.
The species name swindoniensis honors the town of Swindon where the holotype was found.
Its vertebrae were short from front to back, featuring centra set deep relative to the overall bone length with flat or concave ends.
The holotype bones display a mix of features found in both pliosauroids and plesiosauroids.
The holotype specimen, discovered in 1774 at the Great Western Railway Works in Swindon, includes 20 pectoral vertebrae, 23 dorsal vertebrae, one tail vertebra, and various limb bones.
The species was formally named and described by J. B. Delair in 1982.
Paleontologists are unsure of the family classification for Bathyspondylus because it is known only from a few vertebrae.
The family placement of Bathyspondylus is currently listed as incertae sedis (uncertain) due to the scarcity of recovered fossils.
Bathyspondylus lived during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Jurassic, approximately 155 to 150 million years ago.
Fossil evidence dates Bathyspondylus to the Kimmeridgian stage between 154.8 and 149.2 million years ago.
